title: Real-life loudness: the Tiger's own gun buttoned and head-out, its engine, a T-34 firing from 280 m
caption: COMMANDER / SOUND AT REAL LEVELS - OWN 88, ENGINE, T-34 FROM 280 M
input_audit: Arena bench: one T-34 280 m away, 12 degrees left of straight ahead, with ordinary detection, lay, AI discharge, swept projectile flight and impact (no outcome selection). The commander rides head-out from 0.3 s with the Tiger idling, ducks in at 15.5 s and closes his hatch at 15.8 s, then drives buttoned 18-22.5 s. The two own-gun discharges (12.5 s head-out, 24.5 s buttoned) are the disclosed staged_discharge fixture: a round is seated and the gun fires along its current lay while the commander stays at his post, because the solo player fires only from the sight; in a crew the gunner fires while the commander rides head-out. Every level is the calibration's physical level at the ear through the live Audio graph; no voice is placed by hand.
historical_scope: A sound-level demonstration on the training arena, not a historical engagement.
visual_acceptance: Head-out: each T-34 discharge is seen, then heard across the snow the flight time of sound later; a round that misses cracks past first; its strike on the hull rings.
Head-out: the own 88 is the loudest event of the film; the world is duller after it (the ear model's threshold shift) and a quiet tinnitus band may follow.
Buttoned: the engine and tracks are the bed (louder than with the hatch open); the own gun still reaches near full scale, heard through ears the head-out shot damaged.
